For this release, we merged 200+ PRs to introduce many new features, fixes including:\\r\\n\\r\\n* **Auto Compaction (Experimental)** for longer chats beyond context limits\\r\\n* **Remote & LAN Access (Preview)** for easy network access without Cloudflare links\\r\\n* **Faster Chat** - Improved streaming performance, reduced UI lag, and smoother long conversations.\\r\\n* Support for **custom llama.cpp builds**. Toggles for Cache RAM, Mmap, Mlock, Checkpoints, Spe Decoding KV Cache, Vision On / Off\\r\\n* [Unsloth Dynamic v3.0](https://unsloth.ai/docs/basics/dynamic-3.0-ggufs) is released. New Qwen3.8-27B Dynamic v3.0 GGUFs deliver >10% higher top-1 accuracy compared to everyone else. Works with Unsloth.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Auto compaction (Experimental)\\r\\nYou can now do long chats and surpass a model's context limit, with evicted turns\\r\\nremaining searchable.\\r\\n* Long local chats can continue past the context limit by rolling older turns out of\\r\\n active context.\\r\\n* Auto compaction creates fresh context epochs instead of permanently trimming replies.\\r\\n* Evicted conversations remain searchable, with improved fact recall.\\r\\n* Context window information is shown before chat begins.\\r\\n\\r\\n**How it works**\\r\\n* Entire oldest turns are removed only when needed, never mid-message. The saved transcript stays unchanged.\\r\\n* Evicted turns are indexed into a per-thread searchable archive using Unsloth's existing RAG pipeline (store, chunker, embedder, retrieval). Lexical search is prioritized because chat recall is usually exact matches like names, numbers, or IDs.\\r\\n* A recall is forced during eviction instead of relying on the model to search itself. Later retrieval uses `search_conversation`.\\r\\n* The archive persists across epochs, allowing future compactions to recover previously evicted context.\\r\\n* No summarization: it showed little benefit and added ~190s per compaction.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Remote & LAN access (Preview)\\r\\nAccess Unsloth from another device on your network, managed from settings.\\r\\n* New dedicated Settings section for remote access.\\r\\n* Enable or disable LAN access without restarting.\\r\\n* Supports connection addresses, QR codes, and optional auto-start.\\r\\n* LAN access is disabled by default and requires changing the generated admin password.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Chat + Functionality improvements\\r\\n\\r\\n* Long chats are faster with optimized streaming and thread handling.\\r\\n* Projects organize chats, files, and workspaces together.\\r\\n* Chats remember composer settings, system prompts, and model sampling options.\\r\\n* Added prompt queueing and customizable keyboard shortcuts.\\r\\n* Added `edit_file` tool for partial file modifications.\\r\\n* Improved tool calling and MCP behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hardware + inference improvements\\r\\n\\r\\n* Support for custom llama.cpp builds.\\r\\n* Toggles for advanced settings - Cache RAM, Mmap, Mlock, Checkpoints, Speculative Decoding KV Cache, Vision On / Off\\r\\n* Better validation for missing GPU support and oversized GGUF models.\\r\\n* Improved MTP performance and VRAM handling.\\r\\n* Better compatibility across ROCm, xFormers, and flash-attention setups.\\r\\n* Added Intel XPU support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## API + serving\\r\\n\\r\\n* Responses API supports structured output formatting.\\r\\n* Improved recovery when llama-server crashes.\\r\\n* Added OpenCode V2 support for `unsloth start`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hub + Desktop + training\\r\\n\\r\\n* Hub supports more image/video workflows.\\r\\n* Faster and improved GGUF downloads.\\r\\n* Desktop packaging and permissions improved.\\r\\n* Training scheduler and preprocessing improvements.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n \\r\\n

Summary\\n\\nOn Strix Halo (gfx1151), any PyTorch GPU operation leaves the ROCR runtime's `AsyncEventsLoop` thread busy-spinning at 100% of one CPU core, permanently, for the remaining life of the process. This occurs **only with the pip-bundled runtime** shipped inside the TheRock-built wheels (`_rocm_sdk_core`, ROCR 1.21.0 line) \u2014 both the nightly channel and the new production multi-arch channel. The classic packaged release runtime (ROCR 1.18.0, `rocm-rel-7.2`) is completely quiet on the **same machine and same kernel**, which is why I believe this is a runtime regression in the 1.21 line rather than a platform/kernel issue.\\n\\nFor long-running inference servers (our use case: resident TTS services) this silently costs one full core per process \u2014 two of ours had accumulated ~15 CPU-hours each before we noticed.\\n\\n### Environment\\n\\n- HW: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S iGPU, gfx1151\\n- OS: Fedora 44, kernel `7.1.5-201.fc44.x86_64`\\n- Python 3.12\\n\\n### Affected / unaffected matrix (all on the same box, same kernel, same repro)\\n\\n| Stack | rocr in `/proc/PID/maps` | ROCR BUILD ID | Idle CPU after one GPU op |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `rocm==7.13.0a20260411` nightly + `torch 2.12.0a0+rocm7.13.0a20260411` | venv `_rocm_sdk_core` | `1.21.0-local-build-c76140fa27` | **~100% of a core, indefinitely** |\\n| `rocm==7.14.0` from `repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/` + `torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0` (`[device-gfx1151]`) | venv `_rocm_sdk_core` | `1.21.0-local-build-2b22ab01` | **~100% of a core, indefinitely** |\\n| System ROCm 7.2.0 (dnf, EL10 repo) + `torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.1.lw` from `repo.radeon.com` | `/opt/rocm-7.2.0/lib` | `1.18.0-rocm-rel-7.2-43-fc0010cf6a` | **0% \u2014 fully idle** |\\n\\n### Minimal repro\\n\\n```bash\\npython -m venv v && v/bin/pip install --index-url https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/ \\\\\\n  \\\"torch[device-gfx1151]==2.12.0+rocm7.14.0\\\"\\nv/bin/python -c '\\nimport torch, time\\nx = torch.rand(2048, 2048, device=\\\"cuda\\\")\\n(x @ x).sum(); torch.cuda.synchronize()\\nprint(\\\"work done \u2014 watch this process now\\\")\\ntime.sleep(300)'\\n```\\n\\nAfter \\\"work done\\\", the process burns a full core for the whole sleep (`~999 ticks per 10s` from `/proc/PID/stat` utime; our resident services confirm it never stops). Before the first GPU op the process idles normally \u2014 the spin arms on first kernel launch.\\n\\n### Where it spins\\n\\n`eu-stack` on the hot thread (pure user time; **zero syscalls** during a 3s `strace -c` attach, i.e. memory polling, not epoll):\\n\\n```\\n#0  rocr::core::Runtime::AsyncEventsLoop(void*)\\n#3  rocr::core::Signal::WaitAnyExceptions(unsigned int, hsa_signal_s const*, hsa_signal_condition_t const*, long const*, long*)\\n#4  rocr::core::Runtime::AsyncEventsLoop(void*)\\n#1  rocr::os::ThreadTrampoline(void*)\\n```\\n\\nA sibling thread is properly blocked in `hsaKmtWaitOnMultipleEvents` (ioctl), so kernel event delivery works on this system \u2014 it is specifically the `AsyncEventsLoop` signal set that polls. The ROCm 6.3.2 release notes describe a fix (\\\"the runtime won't spin on the CPU if all events are busy\\\"); the behavior here looks like that path regressed or is not engaged in the 1.21 line on gfx1151.\\n\\n### Ruled out\\n\\n- `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION`: identical spin with and without (paired runs).\\n- `HSA_ENABLE_INTERRUPT=1`: no effect.\\n- Our application stack: the repro above is bare torch; no server, no sockets.\\n- Kernel-only explanation: same kernel runs the 1.18 release runtime with zero idle CPU.\\n\\nCaveat stated plainly: this box runs Fedora's kernel (not the validated Ubuntu matrix). Both arms of the discriminator shared it, so the runtime build is the variable \u2014 but I have not yet reproduced on a validated distro.\\n\\nHappy to run further diagnostics (env flags, debug builds, `ROCR_*` knobs) on this hardware \u2014 it can reproduce on demand.\\n\",\"closed_by\":null,\"reactions\":{\"url\":\"https://api.github.com/repos/ROCm/TheRock/issues/7051/reactions\",\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"timeline_url\":\"https://api.github.com/repos/ROCm/TheRock/issues/7051/timeline\",\"performed_via_github_app\":null,\"state_reason\":null,\"pinned_comment\":null}"}
